newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi says rate cut brings EMU closer.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi says rate cut brings EMU closer.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Friday that a half-point cut in interest rates had brought Italy's goal of being a founder member of European economic and monetary union closer.

Ciampi said in a statement after the Bank cut the discount rate to 6.25 percent from 6.75 percent that he saw a lasting trend for lower rates. But he said Italy must redouble efforts to clean up its finances in time for the single currency.
"The reduction of the discount rate is part of a downward movement in rates, which has been progressive and has a continued, lasting trend," Ciampi said.
"With this reduction our interest rate structure is moving towards that of the other major (European) countries which are considered more stable and virtuous.
"This is a sign that our cleaning up of the Italian economy is continuing and is believed in. It brings us ever closer to our goal of monetary union," he said.
But he cautioned: "They are results that must be consolidated day by day. We have done a great deal, but we must persevere, and guard against over optimism."
